item.title: ( Yakkha ): Greed and hatred, From what cause do they arise? Discontent and contentment, Fear, from where do they arise? From where do there…
item.description:
( Yakkha ):
Greed and hatred,
From what cause do they arise?
Discontent and contentment,
Fear, from where do they arise?
From where do there arise
Thoughts and reflections,
Like crows that children
Let fly and then pull back?

( Blessed One ):
Greed and hatred
Arise from this cause,
Discontent and contentment,
Fear arise from here.
From here there arise
Thoughts and reflections,
Like crows that children
Let fly and then pull back.
They arise from craving,
They arise from self.
Like a banyan tree
Grows from its own trunk.
Ordinary people cling to evil desires,
Like creepers spreading through the forest.
Those who understand
That from this cause they arise,
Destroy that cause.
Listen, yakkha,
They cross this flood,
The flood so hard to cross,
Never crossed before,
Without being reborn again.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 10.3

item.title: 'Venerable Nun, in pleasant feeling, what underlying tendency (anusaya) persists? In painful feeling, what underlying tendency persists? In neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, what underlying tendency persists?' —…
item.description:
'Venerable Nun, in pleasant feeling, what underlying tendency (anusaya) persists? In painful feeling, what underlying tendency persists? In neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, what underlying tendency persists?' — 'Friend Visākha, in pleasant feeling, the underlying tendency to lust persists; in painful feeling, the underlying tendency to aversion persists; in neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, the underlying tendency to ignorance persists.' — 'Venerable Nun, does the underlying tendency to lust persist in all pleasant feeling? Does the underlying tendency to aversion persist in all painful feeling? Does the underlying tendency to ignorance persist in all neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling?' — 'Friend Visākha, it is not that the underlying tendency to lust persists in all pleasant feeling, nor that the underlying tendency to aversion persists in all painful feeling, nor that the underlying tendency to ignorance persists in all neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.' — 'Venerable Nun, in pleasant feeling, what should be abandoned? In painful feeling, what should be abandoned? In neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, what should be abandoned?' — 'Friend Visākha, in pleasant feeling, the underlying tendency to lust should be abandoned; in painful feeling, the underlying tendency to aversion should be abandoned; in neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, the underlying tendency to ignorance should be abandoned.' — 'Venerable Nun, should the underlying tendency to lust be abandoned in all pleasant feeling? Should the underlying tendency to aversion be abandoned in all painful feeling? Should the underlying tendency to ignorance be abandoned in all neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling?' — 'Friend Visākha, it is not that the underlying tendency to lust should be abandoned in all pleasant feeling, nor that the underlying tendency to aversion should be abandoned in all painful feeling, nor that the underlying tendency to ignorance should be abandoned in all neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.'

From: Majjhima Nikāya 44 – Cūḷavedallasutta

item.title: Whatever kind of conditioned phenomena, bhikkhus, the Noble Eightfold Path is declared the foremost among them. Those who have confidence in the Noble Eightfold Path…
item.description:
Whatever kind of conditioned phenomena, bhikkhus, the Noble Eightfold Path is declared the foremost among them. Those who have confidence in the Noble Eightfold Path have confidence in the foremost. For those who have confidence in the foremost, the result is foremost.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.34

item.title: Here, Mallikā, a certain woman is not irritable and not very malicious; even when spoken to much, she does not become exasperated, angry, hostile, aggressive,…
item.description:
Here, Mallikā, a certain woman is not irritable and not very malicious; even when spoken to much, she does not become exasperated, angry, hostile, aggressive, provocative, does not display irritation, hatred, or displeasure. She gives to ascetics and brahmins food, drink, clothing, vehicles, garlands, scents, ointments, beds, dwellings, lamps; she is not stingy; seeing others receiving gain, honor, respect, reverence, homage, offerings, she does not envy, resent, or become bound by envy. That woman, after leaving this life, returning to this state, is reborn with beautiful complexion, good appearance, serene, possessing excellent form, wealthy, with great property, great possessions, great influence.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.197

item.title: A giver, Sīha, a donor, whatever assembly he approaches — whether an assembly of nobles, brahmins, householders, or ascetics — he approaches with confidence, without…
item.description:
A giver, Sīha, a donor, whatever assembly he approaches — whether an assembly of nobles, brahmins, householders, or ascetics — he approaches with confidence, without hesitation or perplexity. This, Sīha, is a directly visible benefit of giving.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.34

item.title: Elder Vāraṇa: Whoever among people harms other beings, That person harms himself in this life and the next. But one with a compassionate heart, pitying…
item.description:
Elder Vāraṇa:

Whoever among people harms other beings,
That person harms himself in this life and the next.

But one with a compassionate heart, pitying all beings,
A person acting thus reaps abundant merit.

Learn to speak well, serve the ascetics,
Live alone secluded, with a peaceful mind.

From: Theragāthā 3.7

item.title: The thoughts of craving Are a person's sensual pleasures, The beautiful things in the world Are not the sensual pleasures, The thoughts of craving Are…
item.description:
The thoughts of craving
Are a person's sensual pleasures,
The beautiful things in the world
Are not the sensual pleasures,
The thoughts of craving
Are a person's sensual pleasures,
The beautiful things remain
As they are in the world,
But the wise
Subdue desire for them.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.63

item.title: Elder Ukkhepakata Vaccha: Wealth accumulated over many months and years — The work of Vaccha, now Vaccha throws it away. Thus he teaches the laypeople,…
item.description:
Elder Ukkhepakata Vaccha:

Wealth accumulated over many months and years —
The work of Vaccha, now Vaccha throws it away.
Thus he teaches the laypeople,
Sitting properly in an honored seat, with vast joyful mind.

From: Theragāthā 1.65

item.title: Possessing three qualities, bhikkhus, accordingly one is reborn in hell. What three? One kills living beings oneself, encourages others to kill, and approves of killing.…
item.description:
Possessing three qualities, bhikkhus, accordingly one is reborn in hell. What three? One kills living beings oneself, encourages others to kill, and approves of killing. Possessing these three qualities, accordingly one is reborn in hell. Possessing three qualities, bhikkhus, accordingly one is reborn in heaven. What three? One abstains from killing oneself, encourages others to abstain from killing, and approves of abstaining from killing. Possessing these three qualities, accordingly one is reborn in heaven. One takes what is not given oneself ... One abstains from taking what is not given oneself ... One engages in sexual misconduct oneself ... One abstains from sexual misconduct oneself ... One speaks falsely oneself ... One abstains from false speech oneself ... One speaks harshly oneself ... One abstains from harsh speech oneself ... One is covetous oneself ... One is not covetous oneself ... One has ill-will oneself ... One does not have ill-will oneself ... One holds wrong view oneself ... One abstains from wrong view oneself ... Possessing these three qualities, accordingly one is reborn in heaven.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.163

item.title: And, bhikkhus, a learned noble disciple, who has seen the noble ones, is skilled in the teaching of the noble ones, trained in the teaching…
item.description:
And, bhikkhus, a learned noble disciple, who has seen the noble ones, is skilled in the teaching of the noble ones, trained in the teaching of the noble ones; who has seen the true persons, is skilled in the teaching of the true persons, trained in the teaching of the true persons — he regards form: 'This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.' He regards feeling: 'This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.' He regards perception: 'This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.' He regards formations: 'This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.' He regards whatever is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, attained, sought after, and reflected upon by the mind: 'This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.' And whatever views placeholders say: 'This is the world, this is my self; after death I will be permanent, everlasting, eternal, unchanging, and I will abide like that forever' — he regards that too: 'This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.' Thus regarding, he is not anxious or troubled about what does not actually exist.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 22 – Alagaddūpamasutta
